chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Dawud narrated from his father, who said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Himyari narrated to us, saying:

I wrote to al-Faqih عليه السلام asking him about a man who visits the graves of the Imams عليهم السلام: is it permissible for him to perform sajdah upon the grave or not? And is it permissible for one who prays near their graves to stand behind the grave and make the grave a qiblah, and to stand at its head and its foot? And is it permissible to go ahead of the grave and pray while placing it behind him, or not?

So he عليه السلام replied, and I read the signed rescript and copied from it: 'As for sajdah upon the grave, it is not permissible in a supererogatory prayer, nor an obligatory prayer, nor in visitation. Rather, he should place his right cheek upon the grave. As for salat (prayer), then it is behind it, making it in front of him, and it is not permissible that he pray before it, because the Imam is not to be preceded; and he may pray at its right and its left.'

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, said: It is not permissible for a man to pray while he is wearing a turban or a face-covering until he uncovers his forehead at the place of sajdah and uncovers his mouth for the recitation of the Qur'an. As for uncovering the forehead, we have already explained earlier that it is necessary, and what he narrated further clarifies it:

key_terms.التَّوْقِيعَ: signed rescript; the written reply issued by the Imam عليه السلام
key_terms.الزِّيَارَةِ: visitation; the devotional act of visiting the graves of the Imams عليهم السلام
key_terms.السُّجُودُ: prostration; here, specifically performing sajdah upon the grave
key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: salat (prayer); the ritual prayer performed near the grave
key_terms.الْإِمَامَ: the Imam; here, the buried Imam whose grave is being visited
key_terms.الْقَبْرِ: the grave; here, the grave of an Imam عليه السلام
key_terms.جَبْهَتِهِ: his forehead; the part that must be uncovered for sajdah
key_terms.لِثَامٌ: face-covering; a cloth covering the mouth or lower face

ai.seo_question: What are the rulings on sajdah and salat (prayer) near the graves of the Imams عليهم السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings regarding the etiquette of visiting the graves of the Imams عليهم السلام and praying near them. It forbids sajdah directly upon the grave, permits placing the right cheek upon it, and instructs that prayer should not be performed in front of the Imam's grave. It also adds a ruling that the forehead and mouth should be uncovered in prayer for sajdah and Qur'an recitation.
